rules.summary: Nine teams each play six series of two to five Tests, three at home and three away, from June 2025. A win is worth 12 points, a tie 6, a draw 4 and a loss 0. An abandoned Test is a draw, unless the pitch or outfield is rated unfit, when the visitors take the win's points. Each over short of the minimum rate costs a point. Teams are ranked by the percentage of available points they won (PCT), then series wins, away PCT and the ICC Test ranking at the end of the window. A Test not played for an accepted reason (a security or force-majeure ruling) is left out; one forfeited goes to the other side. The top two meet in the final at The Oval on 9-13 June 2027, with a reserve day; a drawn, tied or abandoned final makes them joint champions.

modelNotes: Each Test's win, draw and loss chances come from a Davidson rating model fitted on every men's Test in Cricsheet's archive since 2001, results losing half their weight every 12 years. Home advantage goes to the side playing in its own country, whatever the series calls home, so a neutral ground gives none.

Draws are likelier between evenly matched sides, and their rate depends on the country the Test is played in and on the era: the rate is fitted on recent Tests, which are drawn far less often than in the 2000s.

Backtest: before each of the 242 championship Tests of 2019-21, 2021-23, 2023-25 and 2025-27 so far, the model, fitted on the Tests before it, scored 0.2048 (ranked probability score) and 0.879 (log loss), against 0.2379 and 0.963 for home-win, draw and away-win base rates. Final-place odds at 25%, 50% and 75% of 2021-23 and 2023-25 scored a Brier score of 0.063, against 0.222 for the table at the time and 0.173 for a no-skill guess.

The remaining 21 Tests are simulated 20,000 times. Ratings are held for the rest of the cycle: in the backtest, letting them drift did not improve the season odds. Teams level on PCT are split by series wins, away PCT, then the latest ICC Test ranking in the config.
The final is played in England at The Oval: England would be at home, any other pair on neutral ground. A drawn or tied final makes both finalists joint champions; the reserve day is not modelled.

Exact claims (clinched, eliminated, can finish level) consider every remaining result, ties included, and the over-rate deductions already made; later deductions could still change them. The simulation does not invent future deductions.

The standings close at the end of the competition window: Friday 30 April 2027 in the Playing Conditions (16.12.4, 16.13.1), the end of March in the Competition Regulations, which take the ICC ranking for the last tie-breaker on 1 April 2027. The last Tests end in March, so only the ranking date differs.

Bangladesh v England (February 2027), Sri Lanka v South Africa (February-March 2027) and Pakistan v New Zealand (March 2027) have no published dates yet; their Tests are placed in the months reported and marked tentative.
